idea.description: SASRec encodes interaction sequences with item embeddings, learned positional embeddings, and causal self-attention blocks. Each position predicts the next item through a dot product with shared item embeddings. Attention lets predictions draw on recent actions or longer histories. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
idea.motivation: The paper balances the simplicity of short-range Markov models with the longer-range modeling ability of recurrent networks. Despite the supplied title, SASRec is not a dedicated cold-start method: unseen items lack trained ID embeddings, and users without histories provide no personalized sequence context.
idea.implementation_notes: The paper uses residual connections, layer normalization, dropout, Adam, and sampled binary cross-entropy with one negative per valid position. For this task, start from sasrec_perdataset, preserve all four dataset routes and fixed splits, use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42, and retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS=200 unless explicitly changed within the search. Select using macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator; no improvement has been measured here. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer whenever inference changes. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), with measured metrics and definitions. Use only available histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    load_fixed_splits(category, preprocessing_seed=0)
    initialize_sasrec(training_seed=42)
    for epoch in configured_epochs(default=200):
        for _, sequence, positive, negative in train_loader:
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)
            pos = model.predict_score(features, positive)
            neg = model.predict_score(features, negative)
            valid = positive != 0
            loss = mean(softplus(-pos[valid]) + softplus(neg[valid]))
            optimizer_step(loss)
    save_model_config_and_weights_under_trial(category)
write_matching_predictor_with_dataset_routing()
# Host independently evaluates working/predict.py.

originality.positive: The original paper established a compelling self-attention approach to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: Reusing SASRec adds little novelty relative to the required SASRec baseline. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Available item text could support a future content-aware extension for sparse items.
future_potential.negative: That extension is not part of vanilla SASRec, and its validation benefit remains untested.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing baseline and compatibility contract support straightforward implementation.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct masking, negative sampling, checkpoint loading, and predictor consistency still require care.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
